detail: self-check failed: acceptance criteria not met or not reported: "A call-order test with a bare remote shows the intent is on the remote before PrHost::merge is called and the landing record after. Run: cargo test."; redacted report: {"summary":"`athena land --pr` now writes a landing-intent record before the host merge and a landing record after a confirmed merge, both on `athena/records` on the remote. The full `cargo test --locked` passed (exit 0), as did the fmt and clippy checks. I could not read the saved test output, so I have no per-test count. Root cause fixed: the records branch used to be written only locally, with no way to build on the remote tip. `RecordsWriter` (athena-git) gained `sync_from` (reset the local ref to the remote) and `append_to_remote`. That function builds the commit on the remote tip and pushes with `push_if_remote_at`, which only succeeds if the remote branch still holds that tip. The local ref moves only after the push, and a rejected push re-fetches, rebuilds and retries up to 8 times. Extra parents are supported, so a landing commit has the PR head as second parent. In athena-core, `gh.rs` has a `LandingRecords` trait and `GitLandingRecords::for_remote`, built from a `Git` and a remote name. It writes `LandingIntent`, `Landing` and `LandingCommit` from `athena_data::history` as `landing-intents/<id>.json` and `landings/<id>.json`, validated before writing. `land::pr_commits` requires exactly one `Athena-Job` trailer on every commit in `remote_base..head`, and otherwise errors naming the sha. `PrHost::merge` now returns the merge method, and `PrReport` has `warnings`. `Athena::land_pr` builds the sink with `for_remote` and returns its error instead of falling back to no records. An unconfirmed merge writes no landing and adds a warning naming the intent. A rerun reuses the existing intent for the same PR number and head. A landing-write failure after a confirmed merge is also only a warning. The design doc has a new \"Built\" section with the `sync_from` recover path, the verification-id mapping and a failure-path table.
